sample.selection: HI-selected (MIGHTEE-HI), z<=0.08, COSMOS; no isolation cut (its own selection is the HI detection)
sample.fig3_digitized: vector extraction from arXiv source PDF, validated vs the paper's own residual panel, rms 0.036 dex

statement: THE EQUIPARTITION LAW ON MIGHTEE-HI (MeerKAT, first use): zero-parameter rms = 0.190 dex on 80 rings (18 galaxies sensed by colour grouping) — WITHIN the declared 0.2 dex bar but ABOVE the registered SPARC benchmark 0.13-0.15 dex; the residual splits into a scatter of 0.132 dex (AT the benchmark) and a systemic deep-end offset of -0.151 dex (data ABOVE the law; -9.9 sigma, n = 72) — the offset is the MIGHTEE sample's own a0 preference (the paper fits a0 = 1.69e-10 on this sample alone, i.e. +0.13 dex in the deep end, and reports its 2-sigma tension with the SPARC-anchored RAR — the law inherits it). VERDICT: SHAPE CONFIRMED, ZERO-PARAMETER AMPLITUDE CONFLICTED at the deep end.  Sample limits: 80 rings / 19 galaxies, all HI-selected gas-rich discs at z <= 0.08 with g_N/a0 in [0.008, 1.146] — 99% of the points below a0 and 90% below 0.2 a0, so the test covers the deep asymptote and the transition but has NO Newtonian anchor (max g_N = 1.15 a0) and cannot probe the law's high-g convergence; pairs digitized from the authors' figure (validated against the paper's own residual panel to 0.036 dex rms); sample alone favours a higher a0 — a selection/photometric-system difference (resolved SED Upsilon_star, median 0.35 vs SPARC's 0.5) that lives exactly in the offset direction.
